payload.adrs:
Five deciding ADRs minted into the ledger, each carrying its rejected options as history and a breaks_if_removed naming a concrete failure.

- se.adr-close-merge-filter - the two-parent filtered merge (merge --no-commit, drop the classified event paths, commit). Addresses R5 and R6. Rejected and recorded: hand-built trees, merge-then-delete-afterwards (invariant true only eventually), and merge -s ours plus selective checkout (silently drops unlisted CLAIMS).
- se.adr-tag-before-merge - the tag is created before the merge is committed, and a close that cannot tag refuses before merging. Addresses R3, R4 and the mitigation of risk R1. Rejected: tagging after the merge (an unnamed window) and tagging at open (would require moving a published tag).
- se.adr-milestone-commits-on-branch - milestone commits ride the existing bless window onto the iteration's branch; trunk changes exactly once, at the close. Addresses R1. Rejected: per-submit commits and timer commits.
- se.adr-event-classification-by-path - the engine holds the path rules that classify evidence, machines and state as events. Addresses R5. Rejected: frontmatter classification (cannot cover JSON evidence runs) and per-iteration configuration (makes the invariant negotiable).
- se.adr-grant-index-stays-on-trunk - the OWNER's ruling, recorded with its condition: the grant ledger stays on trunk as a thin index and never grows content; if it ever carries briefs or evidence inline, the exception is void. Addresses R12.

Three RAID tripwires from the sensitivity analysis were minted alongside them, because a credible flip becomes a watch-item rather than a dismissal: se.raid-tags-not-pushed (risk, OWNER, high - git does not push tags by default, and after this change the tag is the only handle on the record, so a plain push would ship claims with no record behind them); se.raid-shallow-clone-loses-record (risk, agent - --depth truncates the record while the tree still looks complete; --filter=blob:none is safe); se.raid-audit-frequency-shifts-the-balance (assumption, owner - the accepted walk-N-tags cost stops being cheap if content-level audits become routine).

The why for each lives once, in its node; nothing here is restated at the application sites.
